question.text: Which AIF category can be structured as open-ended, and what types of funds does it include?

answer.text: Category I -- Venture Capital Funds and Social Venture Funds
Category II -- Private Equity Funds and Debt Funds
Category III -- Hedge Funds and other funds employing diverse or complex trading strategies, including open-ended structures
All three categories can be open-ended or close-ended

explanation.text: The Logic: Among the AIF categories, Category III is the one that can be structured as open-ended (it can also be close-ended). Category III is the home for hedge funds and other funds that employ diverse or complex trading strategies, often involving short-term returns, leverage and active trading. Categories I and II are close-ended by design with a minimum tenure of three years, so an open-ended structure is not available to them. The Trap: Category I (option A — VC/Social Venture Funds) and Category II (option B — PE/Debt Funds) are close-ended, so they cannot be open-ended. "All three categories can be open-ended or close-ended" (option D) sounds intuitive by analogy with mutual funds, but AIFs are more restrictive — only Category III has the open-ended option. Note: The cited workbook chapter (NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) - June 2025.pdf, p. 237) supports Hedge Funds and open-ended structuring under Category III but does not specifically name "PIPE Funds", so option C has been reworded to source-supported language ("hedge funds and other funds employing diverse or complex trading strategies, including open-ended structures"). The framing above is general industry/regulatory knowledge of SEBI's AIF category structure.
